reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes OneCoin token accounts through purchasable packages and a signup invitation. It presents token mining, early pool positioning, split bonuses, escrow periods, and online training described as a way to profit as benefits of participating.

You can click on menu, then on accounts, then on token accounts.
https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/red1221.
Token accounts is where all your tokens are stored depending on what package that you buy.
Some of the packages that are available, you can get up to 60,000 personally into mining every single one of them so I can get a position early in the mining pool.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not promise a return. Instead, he tells viewers they must read the account note before deciding what to do with their tokens. That note distinguishes a 60-day escrow for tokens from product packages from a 30-day escrow for other token purchases. Those restrictions matter to someone trying to understand an account; neither the restrictions nor the speaker's discussion establishes that a purchase will produce income. The narrower reading is an explanation of conditions attached to tokens, not a guaranteed-profit pitch.

tokens from product packages are escrowed for 60 days. All other tokens are purchased for 30 days.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker connects packages and mining, but its quoted phrase describes getting tokens and a position in a mining pool, not a promised payout. The signup address likewise shows a route to registration; it does not by itself establish what a registrant pays or receives. The speaker's instruction to read the account note is relevant context that the opening leaves out.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Escrow is a condition of participation, not a warning that the scheme may fail. The speaker explicitly ties tokens to the package a viewer buys and describes using them to enter mining early. A guaranteed cash payout is unnecessary to recognize a promotion of paid mining participation; the account restrictions do not undo that connection.

citations.quote: Token accounts is where all your tokens are stored depending on what package that you buy.
Some of the packages that are available, you can get up to 60,000 personally into mining every single one of them so I can get a position early in the mining pool.

opening.argument: Judge, focus on what the speaker spends this segment doing. He introduces it as an educational tip about token accounts, says he is logged into his dashboard, and gives the menu path to the account view. The sampled views show that navigation, an account balance display, and a dated token-history table. This is a walkthrough of where account information appears and how to read it. Mentioning packages in the course of explaining why tokens appear in an account does not, on its own, turn the walkthrough into an instruction to invest.

okay we're here and we are logged in and we're at our Dash Forward here You can click on menu, then on accounts, then on token accounts.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution cites the signup address and the package-mining sentence, but neither describes the bulk of the demonstrated steps. The speaker directs attention to the account menu and token account, then the video displays the account history. Those are concrete instructional actions. A link alongside a tutorial can invite further access without making every explanation of the interface a solicitation.

citations.quote: https://www.onecoin.eu/signup/red1221.
You can click on menu, then on accounts, then on token accounts.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial format does not neutralize what is being taught. The speaker explains that bought packages determine token holdings and says those tokens can be put into mining for an early pool position. The displayed history includes mining-token and split-bonus entries, while the description supplies a signup address. The walkthrough therefore demonstrates the package-based mining mechanism to prospective participants, not merely generic account navigation.

opening.argument: Judge, the record supports a narrower commercial reading. The speaker discusses product packages and a token account; the account page states when package tokens and other purchased tokens leave escrow. The page also displays buy and sell prices. Those are descriptions of a product-linked account, not proof that anyone receives cash returns from mining. The supplied material does not show a required deposit amount, a guaranteed rate of return, or a request for the viewer's credentials. A signup address and discussion of package features should not carry more evidentiary weight than they can bear.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies packages, mining, and a signup address, but its quotations stop short of showing a cash-return offer or a required payment to join a mining pool. Even the speaker's wording is about getting a position early, not a stated financial yield. Treating the existence of a purchase option as proof of a promised mining return adds a step the cited evidence does not establish.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is the paid mining mechanism, not whether this excerpt states a guaranteed yield or asks for credentials. The speaker directly links bought packages to token holdings and describes putting package tokens into mining to obtain an early pool position. The visible account history reinforces that link with mining-token and split-bonus entries. Calling the packages ordinary commerce does not account for that promoted use.
